text:
Owen Power's role has grown more than almost anyone's. The 2021 first overall pick is playing 26 minutes a night, up from 21:39 last season, and has 14 points in 17 games, more than double his scoring rate a year ago. Buffalo takes 55% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him at five on five, almost 8 points better than without him.

He had three assists in the win over Columbus on Friday, all of his points have come at even strength, and his talent range says he is scoring well above where he should be. Our projection is about 48 points, a career high but short of this pace. On the other hand, the Sabres have scored 5.7 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, so the luck has cut against him too.

Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him at 6.9 primary shot assists per 60 last season, 96th percentile among defensemen. Evolving-Hockey had his chances worth far more than his results. At 23, the minutes say Buffalo now trusts him with the job it drafted him for.
headline: Power has taken the big minutes in Buffalo
